sections.h2: What should a Raritan seller deal with first?
sections.html:
Start with the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate from the borough fire prevention office, because a Raritan house cannot close without it. Raritan is a Somerset County borough on the Raritan River, and the same office also inspects rentals, so a tenant-occupied house adds a second set of paperwork.

The Census Bureau counted 7,835 residents in 2020 and estimates 8,516 for July 2025, a rise of 8.7 percent from the 2020 base. The borough is only 1.99 square miles of land, so houses sit on small lots and a buyer sees most of the neighborhood from the street. Buyers comparing a house that needs work will measure it against the neighbors within a block or two.

sections.h2: How did Raritan become the town it is?
sections.html:
Raritan grew around the river and a woolen mill. The Raritan Woolen Mills opened in 1846, became the Somerset Manufacturing Company in 1882, and employed as many as 400 people at its peak, making blankets and uniforms for the Union Army and later the U.S. Army in World War I.

The state legislature first set Raritan off from Bridgewater Township as a subdivision on April 3, 1868. After lawsuits in the 1930s and 1940s, it became a fully independent borough by an act of May 12, 1948, following a referendum held that June. The Nevius Street Bridge, built in 1886 by the Wrought Iron Bridge Company, still carries pedestrians over the river. President Harding signed the Knox-Porter Resolution ending U.S. involvement in World War I at the Frelinghuysen estate here on July 2, 1921, and a plaque marks the site.

sections.h2: How do Raritan's housing numbers compare with the nation?
sections.html:
Raritan has more renters than owners and higher rents than the national figure, which makes tenant-occupied sales common. The table uses Census QuickFacts estimates for 2020 to 2024.

The borough has 3,326 households averaging 2.50 people. About 31.5 percent of residents were born outside the United States, and 42.7 percent of people age five and older speak a language other than English at home, so listing material and disclosure forms often need to reach buyers in more than one language.

sections.h2: What does Raritan require before a house can close?
sections.html:
The borough fire prevention office handles smoke detector certification for the sale of dwellings. Its page says older homes with battery detectors need one on every occupied level, and homes with hard-wired interconnected detectors must have every unit sound together when one is tested.

  • A carbon monoxide detector must be mounted within 10 feet of every sleeping area, and a house with bedrooms on more than one level needs more than one.
  • Fire detection systems must be inspected every year under state rules, so a house with a monitored alarm needs its alarm company or an electrician to put the system on test during the visit.
  • The borough's page still describes a portable fire extinguisher, but New Jersey dropped that item from resale inspections effective February 3, 2025, so ask the office which items it checks before you buy one.

Raritan states that fire code violations have no statute of limitations, which means a violation noticed late must still be corrected. Contact the borough fire prevention office before you set a closing date, and book the inspection as soon as the contract is signed.

sections.h2: How do Raritan's rental inspections affect a sale?
sections.html:
The Property Maintenance office keeps the register of rental properties and inspects each rental unit before it is reoccupied. If you are selling a two-family house or a house with a tenant, expect the buyer's attorney to ask for proof that the unit was registered and inspected.

The same office responds to complaints about upkeep on residential and commercial buildings and enforces the rules for putting out trash, recycling and bulk items. An open complaint on your address can slow a closing, so ask the office whether any is on file.

sections.h2: Which roads, trains and schools define Raritan?
sections.html:
Raritan sits where U.S. Route 202 meets U.S. Route 206 and Route 28 at the Somerville Circle, with the eastern half of the circle inside the borough. The circle was handling an average of 70,000 vehicles a day as the area suburbanized, and the state transportation department has reworked it several times for safety. The borough has 24.34 miles of roads, 18.26 of them municipal.

The Raritan station, whose building dates to the early 1890s, sits on Thompson Street north of the town center and is often the end of the line for NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line trains toward Newark Penn Station. Community Access Transit routes 1R, 2R and 3R connect to Raritan Valley Community College, New Brunswick, North Plainfield and Bridgewater Commons.

  • Raritan students attend the Bridgewater-Raritan Regional School District, which had 8,254 students in 2020 to 2021; about 1,000 of them live in the borough.
  • John F. Kennedy Primary School is the one district school inside Raritan.
  • Frelinghuysen Park, Basilone Park and Elizabeth Avenue Park serve the borough, and the Raritan Public Library occupies the former Frelinghuysen homestead.

sections.h2: How do Raritan property tax appeals work?
sections.html:
Somerset County lists Raritan among the boroughs where an assessment appeal must reach the county tax board by 4:30 p.m. on April 1. The 2026 listing used that date, and it has passed for that year. Neighbors such as Bridgewater Township, which is in a reassessment district, have until May 1.

Petitions go in by hard copy, by mail or in person, with the fee, and a copy must also reach the municipal assessor and the municipal clerk. You appeal the assessment, not the tax bill. The assessment is presumed correct, so you must bring evidence of market value, such as comparable sales from the year before the October 1 assessment date, and all taxes and charges must be paid through February 1 of the hearing year or the appeal can be dismissed.

The Somerset County Tax Board is at 27 Warren Street, fourth floor, Somerville, and its number is 908-541-5701. An added assessment appeal, for new construction picked up mid-year, has a December 1 deadline.

sections.h2: What are the closing costs and tax forms for a Raritan sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. On a sale at the borough's median home value of $456,900, applying each band of the state schedule to the slice of price inside it comes to about $3,761, before any other closing charges.

An out-of-state owner, such as a landlord who lives elsewhere, completes a GIT/REP-1 at closing unless a seller assurance applies. The estimate is the gain times 10.75 percent, and it can never fall below 2 percent of the price in the deed. A New Jersey resident signs a GIT/REP-3 instead. County clerks decide whether to accept a deed, so a rejection goes back to the clerk first and then to the state GIT/REP unit at 609-322-9275.

faqs.q: Does Raritan require a certificate of occupancy to sell a house?
faqs.a: Raritan's fire prevention office certifies smoke detectors for the sale of dwellings, and that is the document the borough's page describes. Ask the borough office whether any other resale paperwork applies to your address.

faqs.q: What smoke alarm rules apply to a Raritan sale?
faqs.a: Every occupied level needs a working smoke detector, and hard-wired interconnected units must all sound together. Carbon monoxide detectors go within 10 feet of each sleeping area. The state removed the fire extinguisher item from resale inspections on February 3, 2025.

faqs.q: When is the Raritan appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 at 4:30 p.m. Somerset County lists Raritan Borough among the municipalities with that deadline, and hearings come later in the year. Added assessment appeals are due December 1.
The borough's Property Maintenance office. It keeps the rental register and inspects each unit before it is reoccupied, so a seller with a tenant should confirm the unit is on the register.

faqs.q: How big is the transfer fee on a typical Raritan sale?
faqs.a: About $3,761 on the borough's $456,900 median home value, using the state's rate bands. A higher price raises it, and the seller pays it when the deed is recorded with the county clerk.
